question.prompt: The graph of the linear function \(y=2x+4\) intersects the x-axis at \((-2,0)\), and \(y\) increases as \(x\) increases. The solution set of the inequality \(2x+4>0\) is ( ).

solutions.explanation: \(y>0\) corresponds to the graph being above the x-axis. Since \(y\) increases as \(x\) increases, this occurs to the right of the intersection, that is, \(x>-2\).
solutions.title: Read the positive side of the intercept

solutions.explanation: Subtracting \(4\) from both sides isolates the term containing \(x\): \(2x>-4\). Dividing by the positive number \(2\) keeps the inequality direction unchanged. Since the original inequality is strict, the solution set is \(x>-2\), choice B.
solutions.title: Solve the inequality algebraically
